nodes.name: Summer sunlight
nodes.desc: The plateau is reachable only in the short summer, and that brief warm season is when its plants grow and flower.

nodes.name: Snowmelt and marsh
nodes.desc: Melting snow feeds streams and the deep marshy soil of the flat ground between mountains, watering the plateau through summer.

nodes.name: Winter snow cover
nodes.desc: Heavy winter snow closes the plateau for much of the year. Bears and marmots sleep through it in dens and burrows.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead sedges, dung and carcasses on the cold plateau and return nutrients to the thin soil.

nodes.name: Deasy's sedge
nodes.desc: A sedge among the most recorded plants near the plateau. Sedges are staple food for marmots and ibex in the alpine meadows.

nodes.name: Kashmir fescue
nodes.desc: A tussock grass of the alpine steppe that forms part of the pasture grazed by plateau herbivores.

nodes.name: Milkvetch
nodes.desc: A legume of the stony alpine ground. Legumes are food plants for the caterpillars of clouded yellow butterflies.

nodes.name: Saussurea
nodes.desc: A flowering herb of the summer wildflower meadows that bloom across the plateau after the snow retreats.

nodes.name: Himalayan marmot
nodes.desc: A colonial burrower of alpine grassland that eats grasses and flowering herbs and hibernates for about seven months. Prey for many predators.

nodes.name: Siberian ibex
nodes.desc: A mountain goat of rocky slopes that eats mainly grasses and sedges in summer. Wolves, snow leopards and brown bears hunt it.

nodes.name: True's vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent recorded near the plateau. Voles of this kind are generally plant eaters and are prey for small carnivores and raptors.

nodes.name: Himalayan snowcock
nodes.desc: A large mountain gamebird listed among the birds of the plateau. It feeds on plants of the high slopes.

nodes.name: Horned Lark
nodes.desc: The most recorded bird near the plateau, a ground-nesting songbird of open country that eats seeds and small insects.

nodes.name: Dark clouded yellow
nodes.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes. Many butterflies fly over the plateau meadows in spring and summer.

nodes.name: Himalayan brown bear
nodes.desc: A critically endangered omnivore that eats grasses, roots, berries, insects and small mammals. Deosai holds its most stable population.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small weasel that hunts rodents and ground birds; GloBI records it eating horned larks.

nodes.name: Eurasian kestrel
nodes.desc: A small falcon that hovers over open ground to take rodents and small birds; GloBI records it eating horned larks.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger that lives mostly on bone and carrion from hoofed animals, and sometimes takes small live prey such as marmots.

nodes.name: Himalayan wolf
nodes.desc: A high-altitude wolf that takes marmots and wild goats and sheep where they live.

nodes.name: Snow leopard
nodes.desc: An elusive mountain cat that preys on ibex and marmots on the high slopes.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A large eagle that hunts marmots and other animals across open ground, and takes young ibex.
